title: Heuristic KV-residency orchestration for ultra-seqlen model variants (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Ultra-long context workloads (>=64k tokens) push KV residency and GPU memory allocation into regime-dependent corner cases. Generic memory profiles are either too conservative (wasting reserved GPU memory and reducing parallelism) or too aggressive (OOMs/evictions that blow up latency and correctness).

Goal: Ship a model-specific heuristic orchestration layer that adapts KV residency targets and per-variant allocator hints on-the-fly based on observed sequence-length distribution, steady-state batch shapes, and model-specific footprint curves for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen family variants. This should reduce OOMs by ~60% for extreme sequences while increasing effective concurrent batch capacity by ~18% and keeping tail latency within SLA.

Scope:
- Offline: gather per-variant empirical footprint curves (kv residency vs tokens vs batch) across representative seq-length histograms.
- Runtime: implement a lightweight residency heuristic that sets target KV slices and soft-eviction thresholds per-request and per-worker.
- Integration: wire heuristic into scheduler so packing/batching decisions respect residency hints and fallback to conservative mode on repeated failures.
- Telemetry: add residency metrics and a small cost-estimate signal to Console dashboards and rollout gating.

Non-goals: replacing the allocator or changing on-GPU slab layout in this iteration; full ML-based predictor (we may A/B test later).
acceptance_criteria: Per-variant footprint curve collected and stored in artifact store for at least Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-instruct, Qwen-14B-Chat
Runtime heuristic deployed behind feature flag with opt-in per-customer and default enabled for internal experiments
OOM rate for ultra-long sequences reduced by >=60% on internal test harness compared to baseline profile
Tail 99 latency impact <10% compared to baseline at p95 load for same throughput
Console dashboard surfaces KV residency ratio, eviction events, and estimated cost delta per-route
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Heuristic misestimates cause increased evictions leading to correctness regressions. Mitigation: Conservative backoff + immediate fallback to pinned conservative profile after two eviction-induced restarts.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample metrics at 1% for low-volume customers and 100% for internal experiments; roll telemetry retention to 7 days by default.
Risk: Per-model artifacts drift with new quantization variants. Mitigation: automatic re-profiling job scheduled weekly and retriggered on model rollout events.

decision_log: 2025-02-18: Chose heuristic + conservative fallback rather than ML predictor to reduce rollout risk (PM/Eng consensus)
2025-02-24: Prioritize Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants for initial rollout; postpone smaller research models
2025-03-03: Replace hard OOM kill with soft-eviction + request retry for at-most-once idempotent endpoints
comments: 2025-02-16 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff done. Collected initial 10k trace samples across 4 clusters. Noticed bimodal seq-length distribution for chat workloads.
2025-02-20 — Marco Ruiz: Implemented offline profiler that sweeps batch sizes and seq lengths; results uploaded to artifact store (artifact://profiles/ENG-131421/).
2025-02-27 — Jenna Kim (SRE): Observed two classes of eviction causes: 'kv-overcommit' and 'fragmentation-hotspot'. Suggested we add a fragmentation penalty in residency heuristic.

2025-03-01 — Marco Ruiz: Feature-flagged runtime hook merged to staging. Test run shows 45% OOM reduction; still short of target due to fragmentation not accounted for in initial curve. Added compact-on-low-util hint.
